title: Xanthe and the Silence
premise: Edmund Marchetti, once the conservatory's most celebrated young pianist, now cleans its floors in silence, hiding behind the name and the mop. When the house where her grandmother taught her to play goes up for auction, she must confront the sentence she has never spoken: that she abandoned music not from failure but from complicity in her teacher's theft of her grandmother's unpublished compositions. As the auction nears, Edmund races to prove the provenance of the scores, risking her invisibility, her fragile belonging at the conservatory, and the memory of the woman who gave her everything. She wins back the house only by speaking the truth aloud at the auction itself, losing her job but finally claiming her name, her music, and her voice.
about_author: Paloma Thackeray is a former conservatory archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the unpublished works of overlooked women composers. She writes from a converted piano workshop in coastal Maine, where she still refuses to own a metronome.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Edmund, working the conservatory's night shift, polishes the concert hall where her career ended, invisible among students who never knew her name. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: quiet ache of chosen anonymity, disturbed when a student plays a phrase she recognizes as her grandmother's.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: A legal notice reveals her childhood home will be auctioned by the estate of her late teacher, Aurel Voss. Edmund returns to the empty house and finds a locked drawer of her grandmother's handwritten scores. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter tracing Edmund's prodigy years, Voss's mentorship, and the night she discovered his plagiarism and said nothing. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: shame and the origin of her self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Edmund seeks help from Marisol, a music archivist who once idolized her, and must reveal her identity to be believed. Marisol agrees to authenticate the scores but warns that Voss's estate has powerful defenders. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terror and first flicker of alliance.

chapters.title: The Voss Legacy
chapters.summary: Voss's daughter Camille arrives at the conservatory to curate her father's memorial exhibition, and Edmund, mopping nearby, hears her dismiss the 'sentimental folk manuscripts' as forgeries. POV: Camille. Emotional beat: the antagonist's certainty, and a crack of doubt when she sees Edmund's face.

chapters.title: Provenance
chapters.summary: Marisol matches the scores to a 1970s radio broadcast recording of Edmund's grandmother playing them, but the auction's terms require a claimant with standing, and Edmund's name is legally buried. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: hope colliding with the machinery of power.

chapters.title: What the Floor Hears
chapters.summary: Camille, unsettled, investigates her father's papers and finds a letter in Edmund's handwriting she never sent, confessing everything, returned unopened. POV: Camille. Emotional beat: grief as she realizes her father's legacy is built on theft, and Edmund's on silence.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The estate's lawyers offer Edmund a settlement: silence and money, the house included, if she withdraws the claim. Her closest friend at the conservatory urges her to take it. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable erasure at its strongest.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Sentence
chapters.summary: At the auction, as the house is called, Edmund stands and speaks the sentence aloud: Voss stole the music, and she let him, and the scores belong to her grandmother's memory. The room goes silent, then Camille publicly concedes the provenance. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: climax; exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: First Light, First Sound
chapters.summary: Dismissed but unhidden, Edmund moves into the house, hangs her grandmother's photograph above the piano, and plays the recovered sonata for Marisol and Camille, who brings her father's papers for the archive. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging earned through voice, not invisibility.
